query:
Company X conducted a taste test to determine whether its new soft drink had a good chance of commercial success. A sample of consumers was asked to compare the flavor of the new soft drink to that of an established brand without knowing the true identity of either beverage. Overwhelmingly, the consumers preferred the taste of the proposed soft drink to that of the established brand. Clearly, Company X has a good chance of commercial success with its new soft drink.

The statement 'The name of the new soft drink is very close to that of the established brand' would most seriously weaken the argument above.

However, it does not mention anything about the similarity between the names of the new and established brands.

Since the name similarity is mentioned in "The statement 'The name of the new soft drug is very close to that of the established brand' ", I'll assume it's not present in the preview.

Step 2: No need to use repl block here because I've been instructed only when necessary facts are missing.



To weaken an argument, we typically look for information that contradicts or undermines its conclusion. In this case, if the new soft drink's name is very similar to that of the established brand, it could be seen as a potential copying or trademark infringement issue. This would raise doubts about Company X's originality and potentially harm their commercial success.
